reason: Verified by driving, and the intent is proven by the file's own history. Measured computed font-size of .b-print .b-away on state=print: 17px at viewport 1440 and at 794 (A4 at 96dpi), and 17px again under page.emulateMedia('print') at 794 - the page box the keepsake is actually composed in. It falls to 15px only at 700 and below. So b.css:1255 `.b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body) }` (0,2,0) never applies at any width where an A4 sheet exists: `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-away, [data-medium="full"] .b-away { ... font-size: var(--size-lead) }` at b.css:1283 is equal specificity, later in source, and a media query adds none. Worse, at the widths where 1255 does win it is byte-identical to the base `.b-away` declaration at b.css:194, so the rule changes nothing anywhere in the product. It is dead, not merely redundant. The intent is not inferred - it is written above the pair at b.css:1191ff: print 'owns its own measure: A4 is 1123px and fixed, so the type steps down one and the scale steps down with it.' git -S confirms the twin was patched by a paid-for fix and this one was missed: `.b-print .b-title` and `.b-print .b-away` both landed in phase 2 (66ef567b), and round 1 (95387db9) added `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-title { font-size: 17px }` inside the min-width:701px block to defeat exactly this cascade - and left the away line alone. One of the pair got the fix. The consequence is real on the one artifact people keep. Measured on the sheet, every ordinary row prints .b-away at 17px/400 Geist Mono against .b-title at 17px/400 Geist; on the phone the same measure prints 15/17, and on the desk 17/24. The keepsake is the only place in the product where the count and the words it annotates share a size, and it is the place where the step down was explicitly declared. Ink density (72% vs 100%), family and column separation still carry the distinction, so this is a flattened step rather than an unreadable page - but at a 9.5 bar a documented type decision that the cascade silently discards on the printed sheet is a defect, and it is a live instance of the lesson library's own 'equal specificity, later in source, silently kills' class. Neither gate can see it: audit.mjs only asks that each computed size sit ON the declared ramp (17px does) and greps source only for off-ramp px literals; interaction-check.mjs asserts print margins, page fit, two-track composition and no title break, never a size relation between .b-away and .b-title.
sharpenedFix: Two lines, and I verified the fix is inert to every existing print assertion. Delete b.css:1255 outright rather than rewriting it - it is a duplicate of the base .b-away declaration at b.css:194 and does nothing at any width. Then add `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-away { font-size: var(--size-body); }` immediately after b.css:1299 `[data-medium="sheet"] .b-print .b-title`, inside the same @media (min-width: 701px) block; at (0,3,0) it beats the 1283 rule without touching the desk measure. Do not also restate the left/width from 1283 - those are correct on paper and re-declaring them re-opens the same trap. Measured with the override injected at 794 under print emulation: .b-away column width stays 84px, .b-print height stays 971.9px (well under the 1123px page), and the grid stays 220px + 420px, so 'the sheet fits the page it is printed on', 'the sheet keeps its composition on paper' and 'no title breaks on the printed sheet' all continue to hold. For the gate, do not assert 'away strictly smaller than title' - that is a ratio, and a ratio is taste. Assert the decision instead: in the print section of interaction-check.mjs, require getComputedStyle('.b-print .b-away').fontSize to equal the same element's computed size at 390 (i.e. the print measure keeps the phone's step, per the comment at b.css:1191), checked at 794 under emulateMedia('print'). That catches this exact class of cascade death for the away column and would have caught it in round 1.
